title: Clapton: Clifford Assisted Problem Transformation for Error Mitigation in Variational Quantum Algorithms
problem: Variational quantum algorithms require accuracy levels that current NISQ devices cannot achieve due to quantum noise and errors. Systematic error mitigation techniques are needed to make VQAs practical on near-term quantum hardware.
motivation: VQAs promise near-term quantum advantage, but quantum device noise severely limits their accuracy and practical utility without error mitigation.
method: Clapton reformulates the quantum problem's energy equation (the Hamiltonian) using Clifford quantum gates, guided by good quantum solutions computed on a regular computer and models of the device's quantum noise. It applies the variational principle—testing different quantum parameter settings to find the lowest energy reading—to get better energy estimates for these known good solutions even when the quantum device makes errors, which reduces how much noise affects the final ground state (the system's lowest-energy solution). The system handles everything from problem to device, incorporating realistic noise simulation during the problem reformulation.
key_novelty: Clapton cuts quantum noise by reshaping how the quantum problem is formulated (the Hamiltonian), guided by good quantum solutions calculated beforehand on a regular computer.
contributions: A systematic error mitigation framework that transforms VQA Hamiltonians to reduce noise sensitivity
End-to-end application-to-device implementation combining problem transformation with noise modeling
Achieves 1.7x-3.7x mean improvement and up to 13.3x maximum speedup over unmitigated VQA on physics and chemistry applications

metrics.accuracy: Improved ground state energy estimation under device noise

limitations: Depends on availability of good initial quantum states and accurate classical noise models; performance degradation when these assumptions are violated is not discussed.
primary_theme: Quantum error mitigation for near-term quantum algorithms
